newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore conference to discuss Asia defence needs.
newsitem.headline: Singapore conference to discuss Asia defence needs.

text.p: Singapore will stage a major naval conference from May 6-9 to discuss Asia's burgeoning defence needs, organisers said on Friday.
The meeting will draw delegates from more than two dozen countries while 12 warships, including the British aircraft carrier HMS Illustrious, will dock in Singapore.
Defence officials from 16 countries, including China, Australia, India and Vietnam, had been invited, organisers told reporters.

"It is anticipated that by the end of the century, maritime defence expenditure in the Asia-Pacific region may well outstrip that of Western Europe and even North America," conference chairman Roger Marriott said in a statement.

He said estimates of naval procurement by Asian countries up to 2010 ranged between US$110 billion and US$127 billion, offering a lucrative opportunity for arms merchants in the United States, Europe and Russia.
"This is a formidable shopping list," Marriott said. "Naval forces in the region are themselves undergoing major expansion."
